recent_works.title: County-level interactions among harmful algal blooms, cyanotoxins, nutrient loading, and population density in the United States (2010-2018)
recent_works.abstract: Harmful algae bloom (HAB) is typically associated with cyanobacterial growth in warm water bodies including those near agricultural areas due nutrient runoff and stagnant water conditions. The mitigation and management of HAB-associated toxicity by water treatment and monitoring agencies are critical for protecting public health. Under certain conditions, cyanobacteria produce elevated levels of cyanotoxins that can harm humans, animals, and the environment. However, the relationship between HAB occurrence and elevated cyanotoxin levels within a water body is not always straightforward. Agricultural activity, particularly fertilizer and nitrogen (N) rich chemical runoff, is strongly correlated with the likelihood of HAB occurrence and cyanotoxin detection. Understanding patterns in HAB emergence and the potential for cyanotoxin contamination across the United States is increasingly essential in the context of addressing climate change, ensuring food safety, and improving agricultural practices as well as water quality protection. Implications of Tobacco Use on Pathogen‐Driven Diseases: A Public Health and Policy Perspective
recent_works.abstract: ABSTRACT The tobacco epidemic remains one of the most significant global public health challenges, responsible for over 8 million deaths annually, with a substantial portion occurring among non‐smokers exposed to second‐hand smoke. While cigarette smoking remains the most prevalent form of tobacco use worldwide, the rise of electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) and alternative tobacco products poses new and complex health risks. Beyond their well‐documented role in non‐communicable diseases such as cardiopulmonary dysfunction, respiratory disease, and cancer, tobacco products are increasingly implicated in susceptibility to infectious disease. This includes their potential to serve as reservoirs for microbial pathogens and their emerging role in altering the host microbiome, thereby undermining immune defenses. This article highlights the multifaceted pathways through which tobacco use exacerbates pathogen‐related disease risk, emphasizing the need for heightened awareness of these harms, particularly among younger populations.
